patch_description:
The fixed optimizer uses Adam with learning rate 0.03, batches of 15, 30 steps per epoch, a 0.90 convergence threshold, and validation-loss early stopping with patience 75. These settings remain unchanged.

The current block has 24 parameters because it uses independent RZ layers before and after an entirely diagonal CZ network. Since RZ and CZ commute, those two RZ layers are algebraically redundant. The new block collapses them into one RZ layer while retaining all 12 fixed CZ couplings. It then adds four independent, small-angle CRZ residuals on the disjoint long-range matching. Because circuit parameters initialize near zero, each CZ-plus-CRZ pair starts close to the successful fixed-CZ baseline while allowing Adam to tune its effective phase coupling.

This changes the block from 24 to 20 parameters, reducing the complete model from 146 to 122 parameters and the gate count from 300 to 276. The four CRZ gates are parallel and replace the depth occupied by the removed RZ layer, so expected depth remains approximately 93. The original hypothesis class is retained while the adaptive long-range couplings can reduce L2 loss and improve convergence.
